overview.short: Nainital is Uttarakhand's iconic Lake District hill station, famed for the emerald, mango-shaped Naini Lake, boating along Mall Road, and panoramic Himalayan peaks.
overview.description: Nainital, nestled in the Kumaon Himalayas of Uttarakhand at an elevation of 2,084m, is celebrated across India for its picturesque freshwater lakes and vibrant hill-town atmosphere. The town revolves around the emerald Naini Lake—widely dubbed the 'Mango Lake' due to its natural mango-shaped contour when viewed from upper viewpoints like Mango Lake View Point and Tiffin Top. Surrounded by seven verdant peaks and offering boating, heritage temples, and panoramic snow views of Nanda Devi, it is the crown jewel of Kumaon tourism.

topPlaces.name: Naini Lake (The Mango Lake)
topPlaces.description: The iconic emerald freshwater lake at the heart of Nainital. When observed from elevated vantage points like the famous Mango Lake View Point on Kilbury Road or Tiffin Top, the natural shoreline perfectly resembles a giant green mango—earning it its famous moniker 'Mango Lake'. Visitors enjoy colorful wooden rowboats, paddle boats, and heritage yachting amidst misty Kumaon hills.
topPlaces.travelTime: Under 5 mins walk in Town Centre

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Nainital?
faq.a: The best time to visit Nainital is Mar – Jun, Sep – Nov. Summers are 14–27°C and winters are 2–16°C.

The nearest airport is Nainital / nearest airport (30 km) and the nearest railway station is Kathgodam (Nainital railhead) (16 km). Roads are generally good; check seasonal/monsoon conditions before high-altitude or remote stretches.

faq.q: How many days are enough for Nainital?
faq.a: 2 days are usually enough to cover the top attractions of Nainital at a relaxed pace.

faq.q: How much does a hotel cost in Nainital?
faq.a: Stays in Nainital start from ₹1,200 per night, with options across 5 price categories.

faq.q: What are the top places to visit in Nainital?
faq.a: The top attractions are Naini Lake (Mango Lake), Mango Lake View Point, Naina Devi Temple, Snow View Point, and Tiffin Top.

faq.q: Why is Naini Lake called the Mango Lake?
faq.a: Naini Lake is popularly called the 'Mango Lake' because from high vantage points—most notably the Mango Lake View Point along Kilbury Road and Tiffin Top—the lake's natural crescent outline forms the distinct silhouette of a green mango.

faq.q: Where is the Mango Lake View Point located in Nainital?
faq.a: The Mango Lake View Point is located in Mallital along the upper Kilbury Road. It provides an unobstructed panoramic aerial view looking down directly on Naini Lake, allowing visitors to clearly witness and photograph its famous mango shape.
